text:
alex: FYI Jordan from Sales pinged about Clearpath's SLO ask — they want p99 <= 350ms at 50 qps for short completions (<=256 tokens). Can we produce a credible runbook/proofpoint?
maya: whoa that's tight at that throughput. depends a lot on microbatching and KV hit behavior.
sam: agreed. p95 is easy with microbatch=4 and fused kernels, p99 is where tails pop.
jordan (sales): we need a number to lock the enterprise contract — they expect p99 guardrails. product wants something we can promise or a clear fallback. :eyes:
niya (product): can eng provide two options: (1) best-effort p95/p99 for hosted, (2) recommended Dedicated config (GPU type + reserved qps) with a committed p99?
alex: yes. I'll run a short matrix: kernel variant x microbatch x kv-hit rate. sharing quick profiling now.
perf-bot: scheduled run started: profile/clearpath-sim-50qps-256tokens (microbatch sweep)
maya: quick notes from local runs: microbatch=1 -> p95 ~120ms p99 ~420ms (terrible tail)
maya: microbatch=4 -> p95 ~140ms p99 ~330ms, throughput OK but some tail events from KV misses
maya: microbatch=8 -> p95 jumps to ~180ms p99 ~370ms, throughput higher but higher median latency.
sam: kernel choices matter: fused-attn (fp16) has lower median but slightly higher variance on long prompts; flash-attn variant smoother tails for short sequences. int8 kernels reduce GPU compute but increase CPU memcpy overhead -> hurts tail sometimes.
alex: pasted short profile snippet:
```
Profile summary (microbatch=4, kernel=flash-attn, kv_cache_hit=0.9):
- GPU kernel compute: 78ms
- KV cache lookup + miss penalty: 22ms (misses 10%)
- Host enqueue/dequeue + cuda-sync overhead: 18ms
- Observed p95: 138ms
- Observed p99: 338ms
- 99.9% events: 520ms (cold-ish KV path + occasional GC)
```
jordan (sales): 338ms p99 is close to Clearpath's ask. Are there config toggles to tighten tails?
maya: two levers: increase reserved capacity (reduce microbatch variability) or bias routing to flash-attn / pre-warmed KV instances to reduce misses. Also reduce async queue depth so single request spends less time waiting — but that lowers throughput.
sam: another lever is aggressive KV prefetch for popular prefixes. In our sim, moving cache hit to 98% dropped p99 to ~290ms at microbatch=4.
niya (product): can you quantify cost delta for dedicated config that hits p99 300ms at 50qps? sales needs cost per qps estimate.
alex: rough numbers from sim: Hosted (shared): p99 ~338ms, cost baseline X. Dedicated (2xA10 pools, pinned microbatch=4, pre-warmed KV shards): p99 ~295ms, cost ~1.9x baseline. If you want p99 <= 250ms we need bigger pool or microbatch=2 but reserved qps must increase => cost ~2.6x.
jordan (sales): send that to me as bullet points. Clearpath prefers predictable tails even if cost is higher. They want firm SLO with penalty for misses.
maya: operational caveat — tails also correlate with noisy neighbors in shared mode. For contractual SLOs we should recommend Dedicated or Private with KV colocated.
alex: proposed delivery: (A) Quick one-pager with two commitment bands: "Standard Dedicated" (p99 <= 320ms @50qps) and "SLO-Backed Dedicated" (p99 <= 300ms @50qps with pre-warm + 99% KV hits). Include measurements and assumptions. (B) Run 24h stress sim to validate tails and capture 99.9%.
niya (product): good — also include rollback/fallback policy (auto-fallback to lower-latency model variant or reduced concurrency) and measurable test prompts for regression checks.
sam: technical note: we saw a perf regression two weeks ago after a kernel update that added extra memcpy when switching to int8 kernels; rolling that back improved p99 by ~60ms on microbatch=4 tests. Recommend we pin kernel version for the Dedicated rollout.
alex: action items:
- maya: run 24h sim with microbatch=2/4/8 x kv-hit 90/95/98% (due EOD tomorrow)
- sam: prepare kernel pin proposal + short writeup on memcpy regression (due tomorrow)
- alex: draft one-pager with cost bands and fallback options (send to Jordan/Niya)
- jordan: prepare contract template language that allows dedicated configuration changes if baseline assumptions (e.g., KV hit rate) differ.
jordan (sales): thanks all. if eng can get p99 <= 300ms with Dedicated we can close. Please mark items high priority. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: run complete: profile/clearpath-sim-50qps-24h -> summary attached (see internal CI artifact).
maya: attached summary shows p99 distribution tightens after warmup window (first 10k requests). So sales should expect a warmup SLA window.
iya (product): include warmup clause and a verification plan (30-day acceptance with periodic audits).
alex: will attach perf artifacts and make the one-pager. Thanks team.
